learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Ocular Artifact.
Apply Ocular Artifact to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Blinks and vertical eye movements produce large frontal slow deflections; lateral movements create opposite polarities near temporal electrodes.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Ocular correction methods can remove cerebral signal if overapplied. Identification should combine waveform shape, topography and EOG channels.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Frontal theta or delta estimates can be grossly inflated by unrecognised eye activity.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Blindly deleting every frontal slow wave may remove genuine cerebral activity.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures Ocular Artifact?
options: Blinks and vertical eye movements produce large frontal slow deflections; lateral movements create opposite polarities near temporal electrodes.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: Blinks and vertical eye movements produce large frontal slow deflections; lateral movements create opposite polarities near temporal electrodes.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for Ocular Artifact?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in Ocular Artifact?
options: Blindly deleting every frontal slow wave may remove genuine cerebral activity.
quizBank.explanation: Blindly deleting every frontal slow wave may remove genuine cerebral activity.

reviewPrompts.answer: Ocular correction methods can remove cerebral signal if overapplied. Identification should combine waveform shape, topography and EOG channels.
Frontal theta or delta estimates can be grossly inflated by unrecognised eye activity.
Blindly deleting every frontal slow wave may remove genuine cerebral activity.
Label first, correct second, interpret last.
